_readme: Seedream 5.0 Pro (edit) — the backup picture model (House job pictures.backup), through the Higgsfield command line. Filled 2026-10-26 from fal's Seedream 5.0 Pro guide and the model list on Higgsfield. BytePlus's own ModelArk pages (Seedream 5.0 pro tutorial, image generation API) could not be read by the fetch tool: every number below carries the source it came from and should be checked against BytePlus before it is relied on. Every entry is draft.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
label: Seedream 5.0 Pro
sources: https://www.byteplus.com/ (ModelArk docs: Seedream 5.0 pro tutorial, image generation API — not readable by the tool)

limits.max_images_note: Higgsfield's own rule (`higgsfield model get seedream_v5_pro`): at most 10 image_references; more are refused
limits.output_pixels: between 1024x1024 and 2048x2048 in total; aspect ratio from 1/16 to 16
limits.safety_checker: on by default; can only be turned off through the API
limits.pixel_exact_edits: not guaranteed: ByteDance notes finer text rendering and pixel-level editing consistency can still improve
limits.price_note: Higgsfield: 2.5 credits per picture at 9:16, 2k (quoted free by `higgsfield generate cost`, 26 Oct). fal's dollar figures were for fal's door, which is retired.

house.use: the same prompt, references and frame as GPT Image 2.5 when GPT refuses a picture we are allowed to make; Seedream's own content rules still apply

higgsfield.references: role image_references; at most 10 (Higgsfield's own rule)
not_available: custom WxH other than the optional width and height fields
mask (an is_inpaint flag treats the request as an edit of the reference, no mask)
higgsfield.differs: extra fields: is_inpaint (treat as an edit of the references) and remove_bg. Reachable through the Higgsfield command line only (the keyed API does not sell it).

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: The words describing the picture or the edit.
inputs.allowed: free text; overloaded prompts drop instructions, so split the work into two passes
inputs.we_send: the same text as GPT Image

inputs.name: image_urls (references)
inputs.what: The pictures to edit or combine.
inputs.allowed: up to 10; more are cut to the last 10; refer to them by number ('from image 2')
inputs.we_send: the same references, in the same order

inputs.name: image_size / size
inputs.allowed: up to 2048x2048; between 1024x1024 and 2048x2048 in total pixels; ratio 1/16 to 16; default auto_2K
inputs.we_send: the frame we ask is 9:16 at 2K

inputs.name: safety checker
inputs.allowed: on by default; off only through the API

inputs.name: annotation frames
inputs.what: Coloured boxes drawn on the input picture, one instruction per colour; each change stays inside its own box.
inputs.allowed: draw them in an editor before sending

structure.rule: Order a photographic prompt like a photographer's brief: subject first, then where the camera stands, then the light and the finish; name lens, aperture and grain.
For layouts (posters, graphics), describe the arrangement like a handoff: name the grid, the regions and what goes in each; put copy in double quotes with its placement.
State composition, off-centre framing and palette: anything unstated falls back to the safe average (dead-centre symmetry).
State each light's direction, hardness and colour. 'Well lit' gives a flat sourceless glow.
Name textures (wool fibre, leather grain, skin scattering) rather than 'detailed'.
For an edit, name the single thing that changes and say the rest stays.
Refer to references by number ('from image 2', 'from image 1'). fal does not formally document the indexing rule: verify on a test.
To composite, feed separate plates (product, surface, logo, props) and give one composite instruction; keep plates in sequence.
Shoot or choose each reference from about the angle it will take in the final frame.
Wrap exact words in double quotes and say where they belong; check each line at full size, long body copy is the weak area.
Refine one strong base with targeted edits instead of rerolling.

avoid.text: Vague quality words like 'well lit' and 'detailed'.
Leaving composition open: it comes back generic and centred.
Too many elements in one pass: instructions get dropped.
Plates shot at different angles: the composite does not read as one scene.
An edit with no 'keep everything else the same' line: changes spread beyond the intended area.
Studio, cinematic or staged wording when you want a real photo.
A person's name, a date or a quote from our own rulings inside the prompt: the model draws it as picture content.
